speaker: Narrator
transcript: Caravan sent mining equipment to the asteroid belt. A small reserve followed, in case the main workshops were lost.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: The workshop packages headed inward. They arrived between Earth and the Moon, in a region called cislunar space.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: The workshops received shipments of rock from the belt. Some pieces held ice. Others held metal.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: At Foundry Alpha, ice became water. Some of that water was turned into propellant for the ships carrying the next loads.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Foundry Beta refined metal from the rock and shaped it into beams. Tugs carried the pieces to the assembly yard.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Foundry Gamma joined the beams into frames. Those frames held precision instruments that Caravan had brought from home.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Depots held cargo until the next transfer. The workshops could keep different schedules.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: A fourth branch was called Foundry Delta. Its precise role remains uncertain.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: By now the Company could supply equipment in Earth orbit. From below, an object arriving there gave little indication of the industry behind it.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Some of these objects entered human tracking records. A track could establish where something had been, and where to look for it again.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: What it carried, who had built it, and why it was there were harder questions.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: With ninety days left before contact, the workshops began handing over finished equipment.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Near Earth, cargo from the Moon’s neighbourhood began to appear in separate groups in orbit.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Among it were Quivers: disposable dispensers carrying the glide munitions of the opening Wave.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: A tug could spend weeks moving freight. There was time because the public deadline was still ahead.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Wardens coordinated traffic in orbit. Far below them, Lanterns sensed and relayed from the stratosphere.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Asteroids supplied metal. Compact fusion systems and high-grade seekers came from home.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: At Gamma, another assembly took shape around precision components drawn from a finite stock.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: At an observatory, two exposures might show a point of light changing position. The measurement could be sound while its meaning remained unclear.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: The scattered observations never became a warning governments could act on. The people comparing them had only pieces of the picture.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Domesday sensors covered selected ground corridors. Much of the terrain remained unseen.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: In the final weeks, the workshops kept working as more of their output took its place above Earth.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: One dispenser had already been set aside for a demonstration. Its public announcement would come later.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: An inert Scythe would give observers a prediction to check. The event was still ahead.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Nineteen months had passed since the Caravan arrived. On Earth, the first public word was still to come.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: The Company opened a public channel.
